topics.title: Nervous tissue: receptors, neurons and the synapse

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the role of receptors and the parts of a neuron through which information is acquired and conducted.
Explain how a nerve impulse is passed across a synapse to another neuron or to a muscle cell.

topics.title: Reflex actions and the reflex arc

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise reflex actions as quick, automatic responses and explain why they are needed.
Describe the pathway of a reflex arc and the role of the spinal cord in it.

topics.title: The human brain and the central nervous system

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the central nervous system from the peripheral nervous system and describe how they communicate.
Relate the fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain (medulla, cerebellum) to the actions they control.

topics.title: Protection of nervous tissue and how muscles act

concepts.learning_objective: State how the brain and spinal cord are protected in the body.
Explain how nerve impulses cause muscle cells to change shape and produce movement.

topics.title: Movements in plants: immediate responses and tropisms

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the sensitive plant responds to touch without nervous or muscle tissue.
Identify phototropism, geotropism, hydrotropism and chemotropism as growth movements towards or away from a stimulus.
Compare electrical impulses with chemical (hormonal) communication between cells.
State the roles of auxin, gibberellins, cytokinins and abscisic acid in plant growth and responses.

topics.title: Hormones in animals and their regulation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how adrenaline prepares the body to deal with an emergency.
Match endocrine glands with the hormones they secrete and the effects of their deficiency.
Explain how feedback mechanisms and the hypothalamus regulate the timing and amount of hormone release.
